title: Let's shape your wedding
subtitle: Eight quick questions. You can change any of it later.

date.title: When's the big day?
date.help: Not sure yet? Pick a rough date and mark it flexible. We'll still build a usable timeline.
date.label: Wedding date

location.title: Where are you getting married?
location.help: State matters more than you'd think. Marriage licenses, waiting periods, and officiant rules are all set at the state level.

type.title: What kind of wedding?
type.help: This changes how much there is to plan. An elopement skips a lot.

option.traditionalHint: Ceremony plus reception, the full guest list
option.elopementHint: Just the two of you, maybe witnesses
option.courthouseHint: Civil ceremony, possibly a party later

guests.title: How many people?
guests.help: The US average is about 117 guests. A rough number is fine, it drives venue size and catering.

style.title: What should it feel like?
style.help: Pick as many as you like. This shapes vendor and decor suggestions, not your options.

venue.title: Any venue types in mind?
venue.help: All-inclusive venues bundle catering, rentals, and coordination, which removes a lot of separate tasks.

budget.title: What are you working with?
budget.help: The 2026 US average is about {average}, or roughly {perGuest} a guest. This is a starting point, not a ceiling.
budget.plannerLabel: Are you working with a planner?
budget.plannerHint: A venue coordinator works for the venue, not for you. You still own most of the planning.

cultures.title: Any traditions you're bringing in?
cultures.help: About one in four US couples blends two traditions. Pick any that apply and we'll add the right events, vendors, and lead times.
cultures.none: None of these, or we'll decide later

generating.title: Building your plan…
generating.body: Laying out your quests and working backward from {date}.
